User.title: User
User.description: Represents a user in the system.

uid.description: The user's unique ID from Firebase Authentication.

role.description: The role of the user, determining their permissions.

createdAt.description: The timestamp when the user was created.

Property.title: Property
Property.description: Represents a real estate property for sale or rent.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Property entity.

propertyType.description: Type of property (e.g., House, Apartment, Condo).

status.description: Status of the property (e.g., For Sale, For Rent).

bedrooms.description: Number of bedrooms in the property.

bathrooms.description: Number of bathrooms in the property.

propertySize.description: Size of the property in square feet/meters.

location.description: Location of the property (e.g., address, neighborhood).

amenities.description: Array of amenities offered by the property.

imageUrls.description: Array of URLs for property images.

PropertySubmission.title: Property Submission
PropertySubmission.description: Represents a property submitted by a user for approval.

submitterName.description: Name of the person submitting the property.

submitterEmail.description: Email of the person submitting the property.

location.description: Address or location of the property.

submittedAt.description: The timestamp when the submission was made.

Inquiry.title: Inquiry
Inquiry.description: Represents a user inquiry about a property.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Inquiry entity.

name.description: Name of the person making the inquiry.

email.description: Email address of the person making the inquiry.

phone.description: Phone number of the person making the inquiry.

message.description: Message from the person making the inquiry.

inquiryDate.description: Date and time the inquiry was made.

BlogPost.title: BlogPost
BlogPost.description: Represents a blog post on the website.

id.description: Unique identifier for the BlogPost entity.

publicationDate.description: Date the blog post was published.

tags.description: Tags associated with the blog post.

imageUrl.description: URL of the blog post's main image.

PageContent.title: PageContent
PageContent.description: Represents content for a specific page on the website.

id.description: Unique identifier for the PageContent entity.

content.description: HTML or text content of the page.

lastUpdated.description: Date and time the page content was last updated.

Subscriber.title: Subscriber
Subscriber.description: Represents a user who has subscribed to the newsletter.

subscribedAt.description: Date and time the user subscribed.

name.description: Name of the person giving the testimonial.

location.description: Location of the person (e.g., city, neighborhood).

avatarId.description: ID for the avatar image from placeholder images.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore data structure is designed to support the RR Realty Hub application, focusing on properties, inquiries, blog posts, and page content. It prioritizes security, scalability, and ease of debugging based on the core design principles. Authorization Independence is achieved by avoiding hierarchical authorization dependencies and structuring data to facilitate simple and robust security rules. The structure supports secure list operations and maintains the integrity of ownership, timestamps, and denormalized data.

*   **/users Collection:** Stores user profiles and their roles. This is critical for role-based access control.
*   **/properties Collection:** Stores property data. Publicly accessible for reading, but write access is restricted to admins. No denormalization is needed as authorization doesn't depend on related data.
*   **/property_submissions Collection:** Stores properties submitted by users. Anyone can create a submission, but only admins can read, approve (which moves it to the /properties collection), or reject them.
*   **/inquiries Collection:** Stores user inquiries related to properties.  Inquiries are stored in a flat collection to avoid hierarchical dependencies.  Authorization to read is restricted to admins.
*   **/blog_posts Collection:** Stores blog posts. Publicly readable, with write access restricted to admins.
*   **/page_content Collection:** Stores content for various pages of the website. Publicly readable, with write access restricted to admins.
*   **/subscribers Collection:** Stores newsletter subscribers. Publicly writable so anyone can sign up, but only admins can read the. 
*   **/testimonials Collection:** Stores client testimonials. Publicly readable, with write access restricted to admins.

This structure facilitates Authorization Independence by avoiding `get()` calls in security rules. QAPs (Rules are not Filters) are supported by segregating data with different access requirements into separate collections (e.g., properties, inquiries, blog posts, and page content). Roles are stored directly on the user document, allowing security rules to check a user's role efficiently.
